summary: Karl Hoffmann was an Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar. He studied at the University of Munich under Ferdinand Sommer and Walther Wüst, later holding chairs at Saarland University (1952–1955) and FAU Erlangen-Nürnberg (1955–1983).

Karl Jettmar was a historian, archaeologist, and scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, and Indological studies. After earning his doctorate at the University of Vienna, he held professorships at Vienna, the University of Mainz, and served as director at Heidelberg.

Karl Joseph Hieronymus Windischmann worked in philosophy and Indology. Educated at Mainz and Würzburg, he served as a professor of philosophy and universal history at Lyceum Hosianum from 1803, court librarian in Aschaffenburg, and professor at Bonn from 1818.

Karl Lachmann was a scholar in linguistics and other fields. He studied at the universities of Leipzig and Göttingen before serving as a professor at the University of Berlin from around 1825 to 1851.

Karl Otfried Müller worked in archaeology, history, and linguistics. He studied at Breslau and Berlin under August Boeckh, Friedrich Schleiermacher, and Friedrich August Wolf, teaching at Magdalenaeum Wrocław before his appointment as professor at Göttingen in 1819.

Karl Popper was a philosopher who studied at the University of Vienna and the University of Cambridge. He held academic posts at the University of Canterbury (1937–1945), the London School of Economics, and the University of London (1949–1969).

Philosopher Karl Rosenkranz studied at Heidelberg, Berlin under G. W. F. Hegel, and Halle-Wittenberg. He held a chair of philosophy at Halle (c. 1828–1833) before assuming a professorship and rectorate at the University of Königsberg in 1833.

Karl Verner was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Aarhus Katedralskole, the University of Copenhagen, and under August Leskien. He worked as a librarian in Halle before becoming a docent in Slavic studies at Copenhagen in 1882.

Karl-Heinz Brodbeck is a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Augsburg and the University of Munich. He held academic posts at Munich (1978–1988) and served as professor at the Technical University of Applied Sciences Würzburg-Schweinfurt (1992–2014).

Karl-Heinz Everding is a Tibetologist who earned his PhD at the University of Bonn and his habilitation at the University of Hamburg. In 1999, he became a Privatdozent in Tibetology at Hamburg and joined the Göttingen Academy of Sciences.
Karl-Heinz Gottmann was a Buddhist studies scholar who was the primary student of Anagarika Govinda from around 1952 to 1985, later succeeding him from 1982 to 1999.
Karma Lek Shé Drayang was a scholar who completed studies under the guidance of Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.

Karma Lekshe Tsomo, a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies, studied under Tenzin Gyatso and earned a PhD from the University of Hawaiʻi. She was a professor at the University of San Diego (2000–2022) and Numata Professor at Hawaiʻi (2023).

Karma Phuntsho is a Buddhist studies scholar and Tibetologist. He studied at institutions including Sera Monastery, Ngagyur Nyingma Institute, and Oxford (D.Phil. under Michael Aris and Richard Gombrich), later holding research posts at CNRS and the University of Cambridge.

Karma Sonam Palmo is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology. She studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and completed a PhD at the University of Tasmania under Lucy Tatman and Sonam Thakchoe.

Karma Thinley Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies scholar and Tibetologist. He has served as abbot of the Young Lamas Home School and Karma Drubgyu Thargay Ling, and founded Kampo Gangra Drubgyud Ling and Tekchen Lekshay Ling.

Karma Ura is a scholar of Tibetology, history, and archaeology. He completed undergraduate studies at St. Stephen's College and Magdalen College, Oxford, earned an MA from the University of Edinburgh, and served as Director of the Centre for Bhutan Studies (1999–2008).

Karsé Kongtrul was a Tibetan master who studied under Shechen Gyaltsab, the 13th Dalai Lama, Khakyab Dorje, and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, while also teaching Chökyi Lodrö, Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche, Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and Khenpo Gangshar.

Karuna Kusalasaya was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who worked as a research scholar and assistant to the director at Visva-Bharati University and later served as Professor of Sanskrit at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University.
Karunapati Tripathi was an Indologist who served as Vice-Chancellor of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and President of the Uttar Pradesh Sanskrit Sansthan.
